About The Apiary Guide

Welcome to The Apiary Guide—a resource built by beekeepers, for beekeepers. We exist to cut through the marketing noise and provide honest, experience-based guidance on equipment, techniques, and hive management. Whether you're starting your first hive or optimizing an established apiary, we're here to help you succeed with confidence and clarity.

Our Mission: Help Every Beekeeper Thrive

At The Apiary Guide, our core mission is simple: provide clear, actionable beekeeping information without the fluff. We test products in real conditions, research techniques from trusted sources, and share what actually works in the field—not just what sounds good in marketing copy.

We believe every beekeeper deserves a trusted companion throughout their journey. From selecting your first hive to managing multiple colonies, from troubleshooting problems to optimizing honey production, we're here with practical guidance grounded in real-world experience. We're committed to helping beginners start confidently and supporting experienced keepers as they refine their craft.

Who We Are

The Apiary Guide was created by a collective of beekeepers with decades of combined experience across different regions, climates, and beekeeping styles. We're practitioners first and writers second—we keep bees, we make mistakes, we learn, and we share what we discover.

Our team includes beekeepers who manage everything from backyard hives to larger apiaries, those focused on honey production, others passionate about pollinator health, and some who blend beekeeping with other sustainable farming practices. This diversity of experience means we understand that there's rarely one "right" way to keep bees. What works in a cool climate might need adjustment in a warm one. What suits a hobbyist might differ from a commercial operation's needs.

We're committed to continuous learning. Beekeeping science evolves, new challenges emerge (like pest management), and techniques improve. We stay engaged with research, other beekeepers, and our own hives to keep our guidance current and relevant.

How We Review Products & Create Content

Our editorial process is built on hands-on testing and research. When we review equipment, we use it ourselves or consult closely with beekeepers who have. We don't rely solely on manufacturer claims or online reviews—we evaluate products based on durability, real-world performance, value for money, and whether they actually solve the problems they claim to address.

For technique guides and management advice, we draw from:

  • Our own beekeeping experience and documented results
  • Consultation with experienced beekeepers across different regions and styles
  • Research from university extension programs and peer-reviewed beekeeping studies
  • Consideration of how advice applies to different climates, hive types, and keeper goals

We prioritize practical information over theoretical perfection. We'll tell you what we've seen work, what we've seen fail, and where we're still learning. Most importantly, we only recommend products we'd use ourselves or confidently recommend to a friend.

Affiliate Disclosure & How We Make Money

The Apiary Guide earns commissions through affiliate partnerships when readers purchase products using our links. We want to be completely transparent about this: it's how we sustain the site and continue creating helpful content for free.

Here's what matters: Affiliate income never influences our recommendations. We only link to products we genuinely believe in and would use ourselves. If a product doesn't meet our standards, we won't recommend it—no matter how attractive the commission. We've turned down affiliate partnerships with companies whose products we couldn't confidently endorse.

When you purchase through one of our affiliate links, you pay the same price you would directly from the retailer. You don't pay more; we simply receive a small commission. It's a win-win: you get honest recommendations, and we get support to keep improving the site.

All affiliate links on The Apiary Guide are clearly marked, and we always disclose our relationships with brands and retailers. Transparency builds trust, and trust is everything to us.

Our Values & Commitments

Everything we do at The Apiary Guide is guided by a few core values:

  • Honesty over hype: We tell you what works, what doesn't, and where we're uncertain. No exaggeration, no gatekeeping.
  • Bee health first: Our recommendations prioritize the wellbeing of your colonies. A profitable technique that stresses bees isn't worth promoting.
  • Sustainable practices: We favor approaches that work with bee biology and natural systems, not against them.
  • Supporting new beekeepers: Beginners deserve clear guidance and encouragement. We remember what it felt like to be overwhelmed by conflicting advice.
  • Continuous learning: Beekeeping evolves. We update content as techniques improve, correct mistakes when we make them, and stay engaged with the community.

The Apiary Guide is a living resource that grows with you and the beekeeping community. We're not here to be the final word on beekeeping—we're here to be a reliable, honest companion on your journey.

Get in Touch

We'd love to hear from you. Have questions about content? Found an error? Want to suggest a topic we should cover or a product we should review? Your feedback helps us improve and ensures The Apiary Guide stays relevant to what beekeepers actually need.

You can reach us through our contact page. While we can't provide personalized beekeeping advice for your specific situation, we genuinely welcome topic suggestions, product recommendations, and corrections.

Join our community of beekeepers committed to learning, sharing, and helping each other thrive.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who runs The Apiary Guide?

The Apiary Guide was created by a team of experienced beekeepers with diverse backgrounds and beekeeping styles. We're practitioners who keep bees ourselves and test the equipment and techniques we recommend. We prefer to focus on the quality of our content rather than individual personalities, but we're always happy to discuss our experience and approach.

Do you actually keep bees?

Yes, absolutely. We keep bees across different regions and climates, managing various hive types and beekeeping styles. This hands-on experience is fundamental to our credibility. We don't just research beekeeping—we live it. When we recommend a product or technique, it's because we've tested it or consulted closely with beekeepers who have.

How do affiliate links work on this site?

When you click an affiliate link on The Apiary Guide and make a purchase, we earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. You pay the same price you would if you went directly to the retailer. Affiliate income helps us maintain and improve the site while keeping all our content free for readers. All affiliate links are clearly marked.

Do affiliate partnerships affect your recommendations?

No. We only recommend products we genuinely believe in and would use ourselves. Affiliate income never influences what we suggest. In fact, we've declined affiliate partnerships with companies whose products we couldn't confidently endorse. Our reputation for honesty is far more valuable to us than any commission.

How can I contact The Apiary Guide?

You can reach us through our contact page. We welcome questions, suggestions, corrections, and topic ideas. While we can't provide personalized beekeeping advice, we're genuinely interested in feedback that helps us serve the beekeeping community better.

Do you offer personalized beekeeping advice?

We don't provide personalized consulting for individual apiaries, as every situation is unique and requires hands-on assessment. However, we do create comprehensive guides covering common challenges and decisions. For personalized advice, we recommend connecting with local beekeeping clubs, extension services, or experienced mentors in your area who understand your specific climate and conditions.
